evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and illustrated in Figure 6A and B.

claim: After the recovery and growth of animals with DTCs in the center of the gonad, animals with the Dpd phenotype were found (2/5 and 3/4 without and with a germ cell marker xnSi1, respectively).
source: After the recovery and growth of such animals, we found animals with the Dpd phenotype (2/5 and 3/4 without and with a germ cell marker xnSi1, respectively), showing that Z1-derived DTCs migrate through but are not pushed by germ cells.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study.

claim: Z1-derived DTCs migrate through but are not pushed by germ cells.

claim: One mes-1 animal (n=45) had DTCs that apparently underwent dorsal turn judged by the outline of the gonad marked by lam-1::mCherry.

claim: DTCs have the ability to migrate independently of germ cells.

claim: Some mes-1 animals that lack germ cells have both of the two DTCs on the anterior side (2/45) or on the posterior side (5/45).
source: We noticed that some mes-1 animals that lack germ cells have both of the two DTCs on the anterior side (2/45) or on the posterior side (5/45) (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and illustrated in Figure 6D.

claim: The presence of both DTCs on the same side in mes-1 animals may be caused by polarity reversal of SGP or DTC mother cells placing DTCs at ectopic positions in mes-1 mutants.

evidence: This is stated as a speculation about the cause of the observation.

claim: After hatching, L1 animals have two SGPs (Z1 and Z4) and primordium germ cells (Z2 and Z3).

claim: SGPs undergo mirror-symmetric divisions along the proximal-distal axis.
